strings.d1.s0.name: Rijksmuseum
strings.d1.s0.tips: Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer; book a timed ticket online, opens at 09:00, don't miss the library.
strings.d1.s1.name: Van Gogh Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: Sunflowers and Almond Blossom; online tickets only, they sell out 3-7 days ahead.
strings.d1.s2.name: Museumplein Piknik
strings.d1.s2.tips: Pick up sandwiches at Albert Heijn and eat on the lawn; a paddling pool in summer, an ice rink in winter.
strings.d1.s3.name: Vondelpark
strings.d1.s3.tips: The city's main park; rent a bike, and catch the open-air theatre in summer.
strings.d1.s4.name: De Pijp & Albert Cuyp Markt
strings.d1.s4.tips: Amsterdam's biggest street market; try the stroopwafel stall (Rudi's) and the cheese.
strings.d1.b0.name: Moco Museum
strings.d1.b0.tips: Banksy and modern art; a good fallback if you have no Van Gogh ticket.
strings.d1.b1.name: Bakers & Roasters De Pijp
strings.d1.b1.tips: Brunch; an alternative to the picnic.
strings.d2.s0.name: Anne Frank House
strings.d2.s0.tips: Online only; tickets are released 6 weeks ahead on Tuesdays at 10:00. If sold out, check the daily cancellation release time.
strings.d2.s1.name: Westerkerk
strings.d2.s1.tips: The church where Rembrandt is buried; tower climbs run in summer.
strings.d2.s2.name: Jordaan Streets
strings.d2.s2.tips: Hofje courtyards (Karthuizerhof), the Prinsengracht canals, and Noordermarkt on Saturdays.
strings.d2.s3.name: Winkel 43
strings.d2.s3.tips: Amsterdam's most famous apple pie; on the corner of Noordermarkt.
strings.d2.s4.name: Café 't Smalle
strings.d2.s4.tips: A canalside brown café (traditional pub) open since 1786; drink a beer on the jetty.
strings.d2.b0.name: Café de Prins
strings.d2.b0.tips: A brown café opposite the Anne Frank House, good for lunch.
strings.d2.b1.name: Houseboat Museum
strings.d2.b1.tips: Life aboard a canal boat; in the Jordaan.
strings.d3.s0.name: Dam Square & Royal Palace
strings.d3.s0.tips: Tour the Royal Palace interior; the square is calm in the morning.
strings.d3.s1.name: Begijnhof
strings.d3.s1.tips: A hidden courtyard with a wooden house; quiet.
strings.d3.s2.name: Bloemenmarkt
strings.d3.s2.tips: The floating flower market; tulip bulbs make a good souvenir.
strings.d3.s3.name: Foodhallen
strings.d3.s3.tips: A food market in a former tram depot; try bitterballen (fried meat croquettes) and Vietnamese food.
strings.d3.s4.name: Canal Cruise
strings.d3.s4.tips: A 1-hour open boat (Those Dam Boat Guys / Flagship); the UNESCO canal ring in sunset light.
strings.d3.b0.name: Bar Brouw Ten Katestraat
strings.d3.b1.name: Amsterdam Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: The city's history; next to Begijnhof.
strings.d4.s0.name: Hortus Botanicus
strings.d4.s0.tips: A botanical garden from 1638; it has a butterfly greenhouse.
strings.d4.s1.name: Artis Zoo
strings.d4.s1.tips: A city-centre zoo with a planetarium.
strings.d4.s2.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
strings.d4.s2.tips: A brewery beneath a windmill; order the cheese platter and IJwit.
strings.d4.s3.name: Oosterpark
strings.d4.s3.tips: The park in the east; next to the Tropenmuseum.
strings.d4.s4.name: De Hallen Kino
strings.d4.s4.tips: A cinema and boutiques in a former tram depot; a good rainy-day option.
strings.d4.b0.name: Tropenmuseum Cafe
strings.d4.b0.tips: The cafe of the world cultures museum.
strings.d4.b1.name: NEMO Science Museum Roof
strings.d4.b1.tips: The free rooftop terrace of the ship-shaped museum; views over the harbour.
strings.d5.s0.name: Centraal Ferry Buiksloterweg
strings.d5.s0.tips: A free ferry from behind the station; 3 minutes.
strings.d5.s1.name: A'DAM Lookout
strings.d5.s1.tips: An observation deck on the north bank with the Over the Edge swing.
strings.d5.s2.name: EYE Filmmuseum
strings.d5.s2.tips: The white bird-shaped building; exhibitions and a cafe, with canal views.
strings.d5.s3.name: NDSM Werf
strings.d5.s3.tips: Street art and container cafes in a former shipyard; take ferry 906.
strings.d5.s4.name: Pllek NDSM
strings.d5.s4.tips: A restaurant in shipping containers; deckchairs on the beach and views of the IJ.
strings.d5.b0.name: Café de Ceuvel
strings.d5.b0.tips: A sustainable canalside cafe; in Noord.
strings.d5.b1.name: Noorderpark
strings.d5.b1.tips: The northern park; an alternative to NDSM.
strings.d6.s0.name: Zaanse Schans Windmills
strings.d6.s0.tips: 20 minutes by train (Zaandijk); working windmills (entry 5-6 EUR) and green wooden houses. Go before the morning tour buses arrive.
strings.d6.s1.name: Catharina Hoeve Cheese Farm
strings.d6.s2.name: Zaanse Schans Clog Workshop
strings.d6.s2.tips: A demonstration of wooden shoe making.
strings.d6.s3.name: De Hoop op d'Swarte Walvis
strings.d6.s3.tips: A historic restaurant in Zaandam; fish and Dutch cuisine.
strings.d6.s4.name: Keukenhof
strings.d6.s4.tips: A tulip garden open 19 March-10 May only (in other months, go to Haarlem); 7 million flowers, book tickets online.
strings.d6.b0.name: Haarlem Jopenkerk
strings.d6.b1.name: Volendam & Marken
strings.d6.b1.tips: A fishing town and an island; an alternative to Haarlem.
strings.d7.s0.name: De 9 Straatjes
strings.d7.s0.tips: Nine streets of vintage shops, design stores and canal corners.
strings.d7.s1.name: Stubbe's Haring
strings.d7.s1.tips: A herring stand on a canal corner; eat it with onion and pickles, a Dutch ritual.
strings.d7.s2.name: Van Stapele Koekmakerij
strings.d7.s2.tips: One type of cookie only (white chocolate); expect a 20-minute queue.
strings.d7.s3.name: Amsterdam Centraal
strings.d7.s3.tips: 15 minutes by train to Schiphol; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Café Luxembourg
strings.d7.b1.name: Spui Book Market
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Friday book market; an alternative to the streets.
strings.note0: Get around by bike or on foot; the GVB day pass costs 9 EUR, and the train to Schiphol takes 15 minutes. Don't walk in the bike lane (cyclists will ring their bells).
strings.note1: Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum, Anne Frank House: timed tickets online only; Anne Frank tickets are released 6 weeks ahead on Tuesdays at 10:00.
strings.note2: Winter is 3-7°C with rain: plan around museums and brown cafés, and catch the Amsterdam Light Festival in December. March to May is Keukenhof tulip season.
strings.note3: Eat stroopwafel hot at the market, herring at the stand and bitterballen in a brown café; coffee is 3.5 EUR, beer 5 EUR.
strings.note4: A coffeeshop is not a cafe; photography is banned in the Red Light District. Round up the bill when tipping.
strings.note5: Take the Sprinter train from Centraal to Zaanse Schans (20 minutes); arrive before 10:00.
